html:
SMTO-SCH-0006 — SMTO doesn't recognise the schedule's time zone

GUID: f9b6e6ae-12da-4445-bfde-4f186ee058bd
Slug: schedule-unknown-schedule-timezone
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • The time zone set for this schedule isn't one SMTO knows, perhaps because of a typo. The schedule wasn't saved or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the schedule editor, clear the Time zone field and start typing your city, then pick a suggestion such as America/Los_Angeles. Time zones must use their standard names exactly, and the suggestions are spelled correctly.
  2. If you asked SMTO in a message, ask again with a standard time-zone name, for example "Europe/London" rather than "UK time". SMTO checks the name against its list of known time zones.
  3. If a correct name like America/New_York is still rejected, stop and report it instead of trying other names. That means the computer running SMTO is missing its time-zone information, which an administrator must fix.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and shows your chosen time zone with the expected next run time.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO, and say which time-zone names you tried. Don't switch to a different time zone just to get it saved, or the schedule will run at the wrong time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The schedule's time-zone name could not be loaded as an IANA zone (ZoneInfoNotFoundError or invalid name) from this installation's time-zone data.

What this means

  • The scheduler needs time-zone rules to convert local dates and times into run instants. The supplied name was invalid or unavailable in this installation’s time-zone data. A typo is one possibility; if a known valid zone also fails, the installation’s zone data needs attention.

Why this can happen

  • The zone name may not identify an available IANA zone, or this installation may lack the required time-zone data.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact time-zone name, for example America/Los_Angeles. If that known valid name also fails, ask the installation operator to check the available time-zone data.

How to fix it

  • Use a valid IANA zone name such as America/Los_Angeles (schedule_zone in events/timing.py calls ZoneInfo). If known-valid zones such as Europe/London also fail, the Server's time-zone database is missing; install the system tzdata package or the Python tzdata package in the Server environment.
  • Choose the intended IANA time zone, such as America/Los_Angeles, and validate the schedule again. If known valid zones fail, ask the installation operator to restore time-zone data.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected zone loads and the schedule preview shows the intended date, time and UTC offset.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • ZoneInfo raises ZoneInfoNotFoundError or ValueError; lookup failure proves neither persistence failure nor schedule execution.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
